why: Doc sentence is verbatim (w27.md line 98, a single-clause <div> in 'Other wins'; no second sentence reverses it). Both cited code sites exist roughly as described, with line drift: the claude-agent.ts comment is at :2045 not :2023, and pi-agent.ts's rate_limited block is at :7644-7662 — the cited :7621-7636 is the invalid_api_key block, not the rate-limit one. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is exactly the 'enforcement one layer down' false-positive shape that inert-worklist §4.3 warns about: both handlers are POST-EXHAUSTION terminal paths, not the first response to a transient 429. (1) PI BACKEND (the fork's default): the shipped Pi runtime auto-retries with exponential backoff, on by default. apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:590052 _prepareRetry computes `delayMs = settings.baseDelayMs * 2 ** (this._retryAttempt - 1)`; defaults are enabled:true (:599429 `return this.settings.retry?.enabled ?? true`), maxRetries:3, baseDelayMs:2000 (:599442-599443). _handlePostAgentRun (:589014) returns true after a successful _prepareRetry and the caller runs `await this.agent.continue()` (:589001) — the turn continues rather than failing. The transient-vs-usage-limit distinction the claim says does not exist is explicit and in the source: NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN (:538149) = GoUsageLimitError, FreeUsageLimitError, 'Monthly usage limit reached', 'available balance', insufficient_quota, 'out of budget', 'quota exceeded', billing; RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN (:538159) = overloaded, rate.?limit, 'too many requests', 429, 500/502/503/504, and more; isRetryableAssistantError (:538194) retries only when the error matches the retryable set and NOT the usage-limit set. The HTTP layer enforces the same split independently: isRetryableError (:106449) returns false for `status===429 && isTerminalRateLimitError(errorText)` and true for other 429/5xx, and the loop at :107424 applies `BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** attempt` or the honored retry-after / retry-after-ms header. Nessy's own host is wired to surface this: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:900-915 maps auto_retry_start to a 'Retrying (attempt N/M)...' status and auto_retry_end to an error only when !success. packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js carries the identical code at shifted offsets. So parsePiError's rate_limited + manual Retry is what the user sees only after 3 backed-off retries have already failed. (2) CLAUDE BACKEND: the bundled Claude Agent SDK's HTTP client already retries 429 with backoff before any error reaches claude-agent.ts. node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs shouldRetry: `if(e.status===408)return!0;if(e.status===409)return!0;if(e.status===429)return!0;if(e.status>=500)return!0;return!1`, with `maxRetries = n.maxRetries ?? 2` and a retryRequest that reads retry-after-ms then retry-after. The comment 'don't retry immediately, surface to user' is therefore correct in context — a host-level retry there would be a second, uncoordinated loop on top of the SDK's. (3) The fork's own error taxonomy contradicts the claim in plain text: packages/shared/src/agent/errors.ts:105-112 defines rate_limited with the message 'Rate limit reached. Will auto-retry shortly.' (4) Secondary: the doc sentence is scoped 'for subscribers' — a Claude Pro/Max subscription behaviour — and this fork ships NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE off by default and targets the Nestor corporate gateway, so the subscriber-scoped surface is largely outside the fork's default build anyway. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist §3. Positive control for the absence claim was established and it failed: the claim asserted backoff exists only in MCP connect / webhooks / session mirror and is absent from the model turn; grepping the model-turn path found it present in both backends.
correctedState: Both backends already retry transient server rate-limit errors automatically with exponential backoff, and both distinguish a transient 429 from an account usage limit — the retry lives one layer below the cited handlers, so the cited code is the post-exhaustion terminal path rather than the first response. Pi (default backend): the shipped runtime's agent loop retries with `baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt-1)`, enabled by default at maxRetries 3 / baseDelayMs 2000 (apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:590052, :599429-599443), continuing the turn via `agent.continue()` (:589001, :589014) and gating on RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN vs NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN (:538149-538194); its HTTP layer separately skips retry for `429 && isTerminalRateLimitError` and otherwise backs off honoring retry-after (:106449, :107424). Nessy surfaces the retries as status via packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:900-915. Claude backend: the bundled SDK's HTTP client retries 429/408/409/5xx with maxRetries 2 honoring retry-after-ms/retry-after (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs, shouldRetry/retryRequest), which is why claude-agent.ts:2045 deliberately does not add a second loop. The residual, much smaller, gap is cosmetic and Claude-side only: pi-agent.ts:7644-7662 offers a manual Retry after the budget is exhausted, whereas Claude's post-exhaustion path at claude-agent.ts:2045-2056 yields typed_error + complete.
